raw_support_spans.text: The radiologist noted that the lesion appeared to originate from the stomach and suggested a gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST).

Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT showed a 5.5 cm × 4.3 cm smoothly marginated soft-tissue mass in the gastric wall protruding beyond the serosal contour, with marked enhancement and surrounding lymph-node enlargement (nodes up to 1.0 cm). Malignancy, including GIST with nodal metastases, could not be excluded.

response.rationale: C1 is the most complete raw-span-based candidate: the radiologist explicitly suggested a GIST arising from the stomach, and CT localizes a soft-tissue mass in the gastric wall. R2 carries the same GIST identity but omits the stomach from the label, making it a correlated less-complete variant. R1 is disfavored because it ignores the CT enhancement and nodal findings, while R3 is only a nonspecific spindle-cell cytologic description without definitive typing.

rejected.why: EUS muscularis propria origin can be seen in leiomyoma, but CT marked enhancement, exophytic gastric wall mass, lymph-node enlargement, and spindle-cell FNA favor GIST.
Spindle cell tumor is a nonspecific cytologic description; the EUS-FNA was not definitive and imaging features are more consistent with a specific GIST.
